newsitem.title: USA: National Media sees losses continuing in FY98.
newsitem.headline: National Media sees losses continuing in FY98.

text.p: National Media Corp said Tuesday it expects its losses to continue through the first half of its current fiscal year.
The company said efforts to restructure operations and cut costs "will not be realized immediately."
The company's comments were included in a press release reporting large losses for its fiscal 1997 fourth quarter and year-end.

For the quarter, the company lost $49.3 million, or $2.08 per share, versus a fourth quarter profit last year of $5.9 million, or $0.24 per share. For the year, the company lost $45.7 million, or $2.07 per share, versus a 1996 year-end profit of $16.6 million, or $0.71 per fully diluted share.
The company's losses were led by significant losses by its Positive Response Television unit, it said.
The company previously announced that its losses and weakened financial conditions have prompted its auditors to express concerns about its continued viability as a going concern.
National Media continues to negotiate with its lenders over its operating financing, it said. It said it has recently received a $3.5 million credit commitment from ASB Bank Ltd of New Zealand.
It has also taken steps to restructure operations at the Positive Response unit, including reducing the unit's workforce by 90 percent, it said.
It also plans other cuts in its global workforce, it said.

"We have begun a process aimed at reducing expenses while making the domestic part of our business more nimble and reactive to the vagaries of the infomercial business in the United States," National Media president and chief executive officer Robert Verratti said in the press release.
